newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C AMATIL SEES ENHANCED 1997 RESULT.
newsitem.headline: C-C AMATIL SEES ENHANCED 1997 RESULT.

text.p: Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd managing director Norb Cole said on Thursday he expected improved margins in Europe and the Asia-Pacific in the second half and that the soft drink bottling group still expected enhanced results for the calendar 1997 year.
"We still believe we'll produce an enhanced result for the full year," Cole told reporters after addressing a Securities Institute luncheon.

Cole said CCL chairman Dean Wills had forecast a flat first half result and an "enhanced" full year result at the annual meeting in April and the group would stick by that prediction after releasing its first half results.
CCL posted a A$58.1 million net profit for the six months to June 30 on Wednesday, up slightly on the A$57.8 million posted in the same half a year earlier.
CCL produced a net profit of A$142.1 million in 1996.
Cole said he would not comment directly on whether the company would achieve analysts' forecasts of a profit of about A$255 million to A$260 million in calendar 1997.

CCL's merger earlier in 1997 with San Miguel Corp's soft drink bottling unit, which generated A$40 million of profit for CCL in the second quarter of 1997, means total profits are seen almost definitely rising.
Cole said margins in Europe had improved in the first half of 1997 from the second half of 1996, as the effects of intense price competition in late 1996 were reversed in early 1997.
"European margins improved in the first half. We think margins improvement will continue in the second," he said.
Cole said he saw continued improvements in margins in the Asia Pacific, while they would remain flat in Australia.

The Philippines would deliver acceptable margins, he said, adding later that he could not say where margins there would go except that they were currently high at 18.3 percent and volume growth was also strong at 19 percent.

Cole earlier told the Securities Institute lunch the Chinese market was covered by three major franchisees, including the Kerry group with 40 percent of the population, the Swire Pacific Ltd group covering Taiwan, Hong Kong and some of southern China and The Coca-Cola Co which covered Shanghai.
Cole said China was under-franchised and under-developed.
"I don't know what's going to happen in China -- whether they'll consolidate those three or break them up or amalgamate them with outside parties," he said.
The Coca-Cola Co and the franchisees would take that decision, he said.
Cole later told reporters he had not discussed any potential China franchises with Coke.
"As long as we do our job in developing existing territories in the best possible way then the opportunity will come to look at additional territories," he said.

The Chinese market is seen the most lucrative potential growth market for Coca- Cola over the next decade as the huge population there increases its very low per- capita consumption in line with rising disposable incomes.

CCL has strong links with two of the three Chinese franchises, having taken the Kerry Group's controlling shareholder Robert Kuok on as a major shareholder a year ago and being 33 percent owned by The Coca Cola Co.
-- Bernard Hickey 61-2 9373-1812
